caption: This drawing, rendered in black ink on an off-white background, consists of several labeled pattern pieces arranged within a rectangular border. The pieces are marked as A, B, C, D, D1, E, E1, F, and G. Each segment is a flat geometric shape with solid and dashed lines, and some feature symbols such as crosses and arrows. In the top right, there is a labeled ruler marked “Scale 1/4.” Below the ruler, there is a block of handwritten instructions explaining the purpose and placement of the pieces and markings: “A and B—top of gaiters. Dotted line on B shows amount of overlap for buttoning. C is part which covers instep, and sews together at Y and the half circles. X on A and C is where strap sews on. D1 and E1 are wrong side of gaiter, and the dotted lines show where D, E, F, and G sew on for reinforcement.” The overall composition is orderly, with roughly sketched shapes, each labeled with a single uppercase letter or digit-letter combination, and short lines or dash markings to indicate sewing, overlap, or assembly instructions. The objects and text are all monochromatic, using a singular pen or pencil.
title: Pattern for Spats
